--- title: "Rosalind: Translating RNA into Protein" date: 04/19/2024 author: Reinout Schols categories: [Python, Bioinformatics, Rosalind, mRNA, Proteins] image: "DNA.jpg" include: true format: html: code-fold: true code-tools: true highlight-style: github --- ## Solving Rosalind problems (bioinformatics)

In today's post you learn how to solve the problem:"Translating RNA into Protein", from Rosalind. Rosalind is a free platform to learn bioinformatics. The first part is a bit of theory, so make sure you understand that. After that I give hints, and at the end you can check out the whole code.

Source: [Link to problem on Rosalind](https://rosalind.info/problems/prot/)

What is the problem?

Given: An RNA string "s" corresponding to a strand of mRNA (of length at most 10 kbp). Return: The protein string encoded by "s".

Background information

Key terms you need to know

-mRNA (Messenger RNA): mRNA is a single-stranded RNA molecule that carries genetic information from the DNA to the ribosome, where proteins are synthesized. It is composed of a sequence of nucleotides with the following bases: adenine (A), cytosine (C), guanine (G), and uracil (U). -Ribosome: The ribosome is a cellular structure responsible for protein synthesis. It 'reads' the mRNA sequence and is important in the assembly of amino acids into proteins. -tRNA (Transfer RNA): tRNA molecules are molecules that match amino acids to codons on the mRNA during translation. (codons are three nucleotides) Each tRNA carries a specific amino acid and recognizes a particular codon sequence on the mRNA via its anticodon.

Translation Process Simplified

Start: The mRNA binds to a ribosome, and the process begins at the start codon "AUG,". (You can see it as the start of your zipper of your jacket) The first tRNA molecule arrives, and binds to the start codon on the mRNA, translating the "AUG" codon from the mRNA into the amino acid "M". Elongation: The ribosome moves along the mRNA (zipper your jacket all towards the top), 'reading' each codon (three nucleotides) in sequence. Matching tRNA molecules with complementary anticodons bring the corresponding amino acids to the ribosome. The ribosome puts all these amino acids on one string, creating a growing polypeptide chain. End: When the ribosome encounters a stop codon (UAA, UAG, or UGA) on the mRNA, the process ... stops. Wow. The polypeptide chain is released from the ribosome.

Visual:

Source: [By LadyofHats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation_(biology)#/media/File:Ribosome_mRNA_translation_en.svg)

Python

So ask yourself: what needs to happen so I can translate a given string, into amino acids? Well, codons need to be transformed into anticodons and eventually translating into amino acids. So find a way to check the given string, create codons, compare it with anticodons etc. If you are stuck, check the hints!

hint1: ::: {#e86f736a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} #Loop over given mRNA string, by creating a codon variable in the for loop. ``` ::: hint2: ::: {#73098606 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} #Use a conditional statement based on the values of the codon and anticodon. ``` ::: hint3: ::: {#88a4ed60 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} #Break your loop when arriving at a stop codon. ``` :::

Watch out! Your input in the Rosalind platform needs to be ONE line. I struggled with this and had to try it 5 times. That is why I export my solution to a file, and then upload this file. Also, make sure to code the "stop" codon with an empty string, and double check your codon_table.

Solution

::: {#ef7a1586 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} with open("C:/Users/reino/OneDrive/Desktop/Portfolio2/posts/RNA_To_protein/rosalind_prot.txt") as new_file: mRNA = new_file.readline().strip() #print(mRNA) #print(len(mRNA)/3) codon_table = {"UUU":"F", "UUC":"F", "UUA":"L", "UUG":"L", "UCU":"S", "UCC":"S", "UCA":"S", "UCG":"S", "UAU":"Y", "UAC":"Y", "UAA":"STOP", "UAG":"STOP", "UGU":"C", "UGC":"C", "UGA":"STOP", "UGG":"W", "CUU":"L", "CUC":"L", "CUA":"L", "CUG":"L", "CCU":"P", "CCC":"P", "CCA":"P", "CCG":"P", "CAU":"H", "CAC":"H", "CAA":"Q", "CAG":"Q", "CGU":"R", "CGC":"R", "CGA":"R", "CGG":"R", "AUU":"I", "AUC":"I", "AUA":"I", "AUG":"M", "ACU":"T", "ACC":"T", "ACA":"T", "ACG":"T", "AAU":"N", "AAC":"N", "AAA":"K", "AAG":"K", "AGU":"S", "AGC":"S", "AGA":"R", "AGG":"R", "GUU":"V", "GUC":"V", "GUA":"V", "GUG":"V", "GCU":"A", "GCC":"A", "GCA":"A", "GCG":"A", "GAU":"D", "GAC":"D", "GAA":"E", "GAG":"E", "GGU":"G", "GGC":"G", "GGA":"G", "GGG":"G",} answer = [] for i in range(0, len(mRNA), 3): codon = mRNA[i:i+3] if codon in codon_table: amino_acid = codon_table[codon] if amino_acid == "STOP": amino_acid = "" break answer.append(amino_acid) protein_sequence = "".join(answer) print(protein_sequence) with open("output_RNA_to_Protein3.txt", "w") as output_file: output_file.write(protein_sequence) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```  ``` ::: :::
